Section 1. Statutory Pay Systems.  Pursuant to the provisions of subchapter I of  
Chapter 53 of Title 5 of the United States Code, the rates of basic pay and salaries are  
adjusted, as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof, for the  
following statutory pay systems:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: (a) The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5 3 32(a)) at Schedule 1;

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) the schedules for the Foreign Service (22 U.S.C. 867 and 870(a)) at  
Schedule 2; and .

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) the schedules for the Department of Medicine and Surgery, Veterans Admin­
istration (38 U.S.C. 4107) at Schedule 3.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Pay and Allowances for Members of the Uniformed Services.  Pursuant to  
the provisions of Section 1009 of Title 37 of the United States Code, the rates of  
monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 2 0 3 (a )), the rates of basic allowances for subsistence  
(37 U.S.C. 402), and the rates of basic allowances for quarters (37 U.S.C. 4 0 3 (a ))  
are adjusted,, as set forth at Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a. part hereof, for  
members of the uniformed services.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Executive Salaries.  The Executive Salary Cost of Living Adjustment Act  
(Public Law 94— 82, 89 Stat. 419) provides for adjustments in the rates of pay and  
salaries, as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof, for the  
following:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Executive Schedule (5 U.S.C.  
5312— 5316) at Schedule 5;

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: (b) Congressional Salaries (2 U.S.C. 31) at Schedule 6; and

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Judicial Salaries (28 U.S.C. 5, 4 4 (d ), 135, 173, 213, 252, 792(b) and 11  
U.S.G. 6 8 (a )), at Schedule 7.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. Effective Date.  The adjustments in rates of monthly basic pay and basic  
allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services shall  
be effective on October 1,1976. AH other adjustments of salary or pay shall be effective  
on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1976.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text: Sec. 5. Superseded Orders.  Executive Order No. 11883 of October 6, 1975.

Chapter 53 of Title 5 of the United States Code, the rates of basic pay and salaries are  
adjusted, as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof, for the  
following statutory pay systems:
(a) The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5 3 32(a)) at Schedule 1;
(b) the schedules for the Foreign Service (22 U.S.C. 867 and 870(a)) at  
Schedule 2; and .
(c) the schedules for the Department of Medicine and Surgery, Veterans Admin­
istration (38 U.S.C. 4107) at Schedule 3.
Sec. 2. Pay and Allowances for Members of the Uniformed Services.  Pursuant to  
the provisions of Section 1009 of Title 37 of the United States Code, the rates of  
monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 2 0 3 (a )), the rates of basic allowances for subsistence  
(37 U.S.C. 402), and the rates of basic allowances for quarters (37 U.S.C. 4 0 3 (a ))  
are adjusted,, as set forth at Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a. part hereof, for  
members of the uniformed services.
Sec. 3. Executive Salaries.  The Executive Salary Cost of Living Adjustment Act  
(Public Law 94— 82, 89 Stat. 419) provides for adjustments in the rates of pay and  
salaries, as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof, for the  
following:
(a) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Executive Schedule (5 U.S.C.  
5312— 5316) at Schedule 5;
(b) Congressional Salaries (2 U.S.C. 31) at Schedule 6; and
(c) Judicial Salaries (28 U.S.C. 5, 4 4 (d ), 135, 173, 213, 252, 792(b) and 11  
U.S.G. 6 8 (a )), at Schedule 7.
Sec. 4. Effective Date.  The adjustments in rates of monthly basic pay and basic  
allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services shall  
be effective on October 1,1976. AH other adjustments of salary or pay shall be effective  
on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1976.
Sec. 5. Superseded Orders.  Executive Order No. 11883 of October 6, 1975.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11941 of October 1, 1976 (official text 41 FR 43889-43894, saved OCR text layer read in full: five sections and seven rate schedules ending with the filing line) adjusts statutory pay systems (s.1, Schedules 1-3), uniformed-services pay and allowances (s.2, Schedule 4) and executive, congressional and judicial salaries (s.3, Schedules 5-7), sets effective dates (s.4) and supersedes EO 11883 (s.5). Each schedule is inventoried as its own clause (heading quoted; the tables themselves are the operative rates). EO 11943 (October 25, 1976) corrected one figure in Schedule 3 (later event). EO 12010 of September 28, 1977 (42 FR 52365, read in full) section 4: 'Executive Order No. 11941 of October 1, 1976, is superseded', so every clause is terminated, but its rates take effect on pay-period dates that the held sources do not fix, and it does not cover Schedules 5-7. The current-law lead (28 U.S.C. 172 note) is a historical salary note ('formerly set out as a note under section 5332 of Title 5'), not a continuing basis, so it does not contradict the NO status. No first-end date is asserted. Partial claim.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12010 contains no savings clause for EO 11941; it sets new rates under its own schedules. Pay and allowances already paid at the 1976 rates are completed payments, not continuing effects; the order created no fund, office, property or vested right beyond pay for periods already served.

unresolved_material_gaps: First end not established for sections 1, 2 and 4 and Schedules 1-4: EO 12010 section 4 supersedes EO 11941, and its section 3 makes the new uniformed-services rates effective October 1, 1977 but all other new rates effective 'on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1977', which is not a single calendar date and is not fixed by any held source; when the supersession itself took effect (signing, September 28, 1977, or the new rates' dates) is also not settled.

First end not established for section 3 and Schedules 5-7 (Vice President, Executive Schedule, congressional and judicial salaries): EO 12010 does not re-set these rates, so they may have been displaced earlier by a separate 1977 salary adjustment; no held source shows when they were replaced.
claim.research_rationale: EO 11941 of October 1, 1976 (official text 41 FR 43889-43894, saved OCR text layer read in full: five sections and seven rate schedules ending with the filing line) adjusts statutory pay systems (s.1, Schedules 1-3), uniformed-services pay and allowances (s.2, Schedule 4) and executive, congressional and judicial salaries (s.3, Schedules 5-7), sets effective dates (s.4) and supersedes EO 11883 (s.5). Each schedule is inventoried as its own clause (heading quoted; the tables themselves are the operative rates). EO 11943 (October 25, 1976) corrected one figure in Schedule 3 (later event). EO 12010 of September 28, 1977 (42 FR 52365, read in full) section 4: 'Executive Order No. 11941 of October 1, 1976, is superseded', so every clause is terminated, but its rates take effect on pay-period dates that the held sources do not fix, and it does not cover Schedules 5-7. The current-law lead (28 U.S.C. 172 note) is a historical salary note ('formerly set out as a note under section 5332 of Title 5'), not a continuing basis, so it does not contradict the NO status. No first-end date is asserted. Partial claim.
